summary: Nordmark group motor maker (4,800 staff, stable credit); we are 0.23 % of its turnover. Asks +6.5 % on the 7.5 kW motor (348.32 to 370.96) citing copper; notice was on time. Price already 7 % below its should-cost. Arena: 10/10 deals, about 362-366 with a CU-NOTATION index clause, about 372 without. Trade an index clause plus binding volume rather than argue.
notes: Fears carrying copper risk and below-cost pricing. Asks above 2 % go to a pricing committee. It cites rising CU, LCI-C and PPI as cost drivers. It never shares a calculation; one arena reply promising a breakdown was LLM filler. The letter's 'reliably for many years' clashes with OTD of 83-94 %, below the 95 % target.

evidence.quote: price changes above 2 % need the approval of their pricing committee, which meets every two weeks.
We agree to your proposed index clause on CU-NOTATION, which allows us to remove the material risk premium
Implementing this index clause aligns with our requirement to manage raw material volatility

levers: shorter payment term for a lower price
avoid: citing copper, LCI-C or PPI (they rose)
claiming a notice breach (letter was on time)
changing terms after a final offer
tactics: Open deep at the current 348.32; the first counter does not depend on the opening.
Offer a CU-NOTATION index clause (material share 0.2, deadband 5 %): it then drops its risk premium; all 6 index deals in the arena sample closed at 361.7-366.0.
Pair the index clause with a stated binding annual volume; it asks for one every time.
Send the volume data it asks for; it confirms the data and takes it into account.
Do not ask for 90-day payment without the index; it raised the price to about 373 for that.
playbook.expected_concession: From 370.96 it reaches about 362-366 within 1-4 rounds with the index clause; without one it holds near 372 and sends a final offer around round 4.
